title: Portfolio Construction
answer: Personalised advice, optimisation, tail risk hedging, sustainability factors and pricing illiquid assets.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice is the practice of shaping a portfolio around one household's goals, tax position, time horizon, liquidity needs and tolerance for loss.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance covers methods that treat risk as more than the standard deviation of returns.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in portfolio construction covers the deliberate use of instruments and overlays to limit losses from rare, severe market moves, such as crashes, volatility spikes, or correlation breakdowns.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios are the environmental, social and governance characteristics of holdings that investors use alongside financial measures.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, and stakes in private companies.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of deciding what a person or institution should hold, in what amounts, and why. Artificial intelligence is now used across that work in several concrete ways: models estimate expected returns and correlations from large datasets, optimisers search over allocations under constraints, and language models help turn a client's stated goals into a starting portfolio. Robo advisory services run these pipelines end to end, and institutional desks use machine learning to forecast risk and to screen holdings for environmental, social and governance criteria. The field is not one method but a stack, from data cleaning through forecasting to the final trade list.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature. Mean variance optimisation is standard, and machine learning extensions that handle skewness, fat tails and regime shifts are well studied and widely deployed. Tail risk hedging has real tools, from options overlays to models that estimate drawdown probabilities, though no method reliably predicts the timing of a crash. Sustainability factors are measurable but inconsistent across data providers, and scores disagree, which limits how much weight they can carry. Pricing illiquid assets remains the weakest area: private credit, real estate and stakes in unlisted companies have few transactions, so any model output is an estimate with wide error bars, and the honest limit is that AI cannot manufacture liquidity or a true market price where none exists.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Personalised Wealth Advice for how client goals, risk tolerance and constraints become an actual allocation, including where automation ends and human judgement begins. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance goes deeper into the mathematics, covering how models handle non normal returns and the practical cost of estimation error. Tail Risk Hedging then addresses what happens when those assumptions break, looking at hedging instruments and the difficulty of protecting against rare events. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios covers the data and scoring problems behind ESG tilts, and Pricing Illiquid Assets closes the set by examining valuation when markets are thin or absent. Together the pages move from the individual client to the optimiser to the extremes of risk, then to the two areas where data quality most limits what AI can claim.
